name: pulse-tailwind-design-system
description: Applies Tailwind CSS 4 design-system rules to React components in this Laravel app. Use when styling components, variants, typography, spacing, colors, dark mode, shadows, responsive layout, tokens, or theme utilities.
purpose: Prevent one-off styling, token drift, inaccessible colour choices, and responsive layout instability.
single_responsibility: Tailwind CSS 4 styling of components against the design system: semantic tokens, finite variants, responsive layout, dark mode, and visual consistency.
triggers: Styling a reusable component or page section
Adding variants, sizes, shadows, radius, focus states, or dark mode
Creating or using Tailwind CSS 4 tokens
completion_criteria: Semantic tokens and existing utilities are used before any new value
Classes follow local merge-helper conventions and arbitrary values stay rare and justified
Variants and sizes are finite and typed
Responsive behaviour is explicit across supported breakpoints
Light and dark variants preserve contrast and hierarchy
validation_criteria: Layout holds on mobile and desktop
Styling does not create a parallel visual system
failure_handling: If consistent styling cannot be achieved without inventing a parallel visual system or drifting from existing tokens, stop and report the token/design gap instead of shipping one-off styles.
Report any variant, token, or responsive decision left unresolved because conventions or breakpoints are unknown.
escalation_path: Route uncertain Tailwind CSS 4 token or utility behaviour through pulse-docs-research.
Escalate to the user when new design tokens, a design reference, or a visual-direction decision is required.
Hand contrast and focus semantics to pulse-accessibility-wcag and animation styling to pulse-motion-interactions.
responsibilities: Use semantic tokens and existing utilities.
Maintain typography, spacing, radius, shadow, border, and focus consistency.
Ensure responsive layout and text wrapping hold.
Use Tailwind `dark:` and responsive variants intentionally together when both states must be supported.
non_responsibilities: Component API design beyond variant naming.
Accessibility semantics, though contrast and focus are shared concerns.
